source.note: Reverse-engineered catalogue. Keep the original project attribution and verify unusual parameter mappings on hardware where needed.

musical_profile.what_it_does: ISP Decimator-style noise gate/reduction that attenuates signal below a threshold.
character: can sound abrupt if set too aggressively
best_for: cleaning up hiss/hum ahead of high-gain drive or amp stages
watch_out: too high a threshold chokes sustain and can clip the tail off notes/chords

musical_profile.what_it_does: Xotic BB Preamp-style clean boost that can also push into light overdrive as Gain rises.
character: transparent clean lift at low Gain
warm mid-forward drive as Gain rises
watch_out: higher Gain settings start colouring the tone rather than staying purely clean

musical_profile.what_it_does: Xotic EP Booster-style treble-forward boost modelled on an Echoplex preamp stage.
character: adds perceived volume without much added gain
watch_out: the Bright switch can be too much treble into an already bright amp

musical_profile.what_it_does: MXR Micro Amp-style simple clean gain boost.
character: mostly adds level and a touch of body
best_for: driving the front of an amp harder without changing its EQ character
watch_out: single-knob design means no tone shaping — pair with a separate EQ if needed

musical_profile.what_it_does: Ross Compressor-style sustain and level evening, a classic simple three-knob squash compressor.
watch_out: higher Sustain settings noticeably flatten pick dynamics

semantic.low: faster attack — catches more of the pick transient into the compressor, sounding more squashed
semantic.high: slower attack — lets more of the initial pick transient through uncompressed

musical_profile.what_it_does: Keeley Compressor-style level evening and sustain, with an Attack control that can retain or soften the pick transient.
character: can support clean parts transparently, or add obvious compression and sustain
watch_out: fast Attack settings can noticeably soften pick definition

semantic.function: sets the lower bound of the filter sweep range
sets the upper bound of the filter sweep range

musical_profile.what_it_does: Envelope/rate-driven filter sweep in the vein of an auto-wah or resonant filter effect.
watch_out: origin/circuit is not documented — treat as a generic filter effect, not a specific pedal clone

semantic.function: selects the envelope filter's sweep behaviour

musical_profile.what_it_does: Envelope-following filter (auto-wah style) that opens with picking dynamics.
watch_out: origin/circuit is not documented — treat as a generic envelope filter, not a specific pedal clone

musical_profile.what_it_does: Detune/unison-style pitch effect that blends a slightly detuned voice with the dry signal.
character: chorus-adjacent but pitch-based rather than modulated
watch_out: too much Wet can sound out of tune rather than thick

musical_profile.what_it_does: Clean octave generator adding an octave-down and/or octave-up voice to the dry signal.
character: clean tracking octaver rather than a fuzz-octave effect
watch_out: fast lines and full chords can produce tracking artifacts

musical_profile.what_it_does: Harmony/pitch-shifter adding a high and/or low interval voice above and below the dry signal.
character: can sound synthetic if the interval doesn't fit the key
watch_out: fixed-interval harmony can clash outside the key it was set up for

semantic.function: selects between alternate acoustic body/voicing character presets

musical_profile.what_it_does: Acoustic-simulator voicing that re-shapes an electric guitar signal to sound more like a piezo/acoustic instrument.
character: less compressed than a typical electric amp voicing
best_for: acoustic-style parts played on an electric guitar
watch_out: only choose when the requested tone specifically needs an acoustic voicing

semantic.function: sets the parked/manual sweep position when not using an expression pedal

musical_profile.what_it_does: Dunlop Cry Baby-style wah pedal with a classic vocal sweep.
watch_out: a wah left parked mid-sweep can sound nasal — favour it as a swept, played effect

musical_profile.what_it_does: Boss ODB-3-style bass overdrive with a Blend control to mix clean low end under the driven signal.
character: retains low-end weight via the clean blend
best_for: bass drive/grit that needs to keep low-end authority
watch_out: too little Blend can leave the low end thin under a full band mix

semantic.function: low-pass filter that works in the opposite sense to a typical tone/treble knob
semantic.low: brighter, more high-frequency content passes through — less filtering
semantic.high: darker — more high-frequency content is filtered out

musical_profile.what_it_does: ProCo RAT-style distortion (LM308 op-amp version) with a single-knob Filter tone control.
best_for: tightening a low-gain amp into believable drive
watch_out: the Filter control works in reverse of a normal tone knob — see its parameter note

musical_profile.what_it_does: MI Audio Crunch Box-style distortion voiced to sound like a cranked amp rather than a fizzy pedal.
best_for: tightening a clean amp into believable crunch

musical_profile.what_it_does: MXR Distortion+-style op-amp hard-clipping distortion, one of the earliest classic distortion pedal designs.

musical_profile.what_it_does: Boss DS-1-style distortion, a classic mid-boosted hard-clipping pedal.

musical_profile.what_it_does: Dallas-Arbiter Fuzz Face-style germanium fuzz.
character: cleans up and gates as guitar volume is lowered
best_for: vintage psychedelic/classic-rock fuzz leads with dynamic volume-knob cleanup

Gate.what_it_does: Attenuates the signal below a threshold to silence noise and hum between notes.
best_for: cleaning up hiss on silent passages
watch_out: too high a threshold chokes sustain and clips the tail of notes/chords

Boost.what_it_does: Raises signal level, and/or pushes the following gain stage harder, generally without adding much of its own clipping.
best_for: tightening/pushing an amp or drive pedal
watch_out: can overload a following drive stage or clip an already hot amp input

Comp.what_it_does: Evens out note-to-note volume and adds sustain by reducing dynamic range.
character: can be transparent support or deliberately squashed
watch_out: too much can flatten pick dynamics and reduce headroom

Filter.what_it_does: Shapes frequency response dynamically (envelope-following) or statically for wah/synth-style colour.
watch_out: aggressive settings can sound thin or gimmicky outside funk/synth contexts

Pitch.what_it_does: Adds octave, harmony, or detune voices alongside (or instead of) the dry signal.
watch_out: tracking artifacts can appear on fast lines or full chords

Sim.what_it_does: Re-voices the instrument's character, such as making an electric guitar sound more acoustic.
character: transformative rather than a subtle colour
best_for: unplugged-style textures from an electric guitar
watch_out: only appropriate when the request specifically calls for a re-voiced instrument character

Wah.what_it_does: Sweeps a resonant frequency peak, either by treadle or fixed setting.
watch_out: overuse, or a static wah left mid-sweep, can sound gimmicky or nasal

OD.what_it_does: Adds low-to-medium gain clipping, generally more dynamic and touch-sensitive than distortion.
watch_out: too much gain can reduce articulation and dynamic response

Distortion.what_it_does: Adds stronger, more saturated clipping than overdrive, with denser sustain.
watch_out: can reduce pick dynamics and note separation at high gain

Fuzz.what_it_does: Creates heavily saturated, often gated or splatty clipping with a deliberately rough or vintage character.
watch_out: can be loose, splatty or gated in ways that don't suit precise clean parts

Bass Drive.what_it_does: Adds drive voiced to retain low-frequency weight while adding grit.
best_for: bass grit and growl that needs to sit under a full band mix
watch_out: too much gain can thin out the fundamental low end if not blended with clean signal

Acoustic.what_it_does: Voices an electric guitar signal to behave more like an acoustic/piezo instrument through the amp stage.
character: less compressed than a typical electric amp voicing
best_for: acoustic-style parts played on an electric guitar
watch_out: only choose when the requested tone is specifically acoustic-voiced

Bass.what_it_does: An amp voicing built around bass-guitar frequencies, headroom and dynamics.
character: amp voicing rather than a guitar amp's midrange emphasis
best_for: bass tone shaping for rock, studio, or vintage styles depending on the model
watch_out: not a substitute for a guitar amp voicing even at similar gain settings

Clean.what_it_does: High-headroom or low-gain amp voicing intended to stay clean until pushed hard.
character: responsive to pick attack and guitar volume
best_for: a pedal platform for external drive/boost
country, funk, jazz and ambient tones
watch_out: some models colour the clean tone strongly (scooped, chimey, etc.) — match to the requested voicing

Drive.what_it_does: Amp voicing with natural, amp-like breakup and medium gain.
character: less saturated than a high-gain amp
watch_out: pushing gain far past its designed range can sound thin or fizzy compared to a purpose-built high-gain amp

Hi Gain.what_it_does: High-gain amp voicing built for saturated, sustained rock and metal tones.
character: usually tight and controlled at the low end
watch_out: excess gain/low-end can turn muddy without a tight cab and disciplined EQ

Bass Cab.what_it_does: Cabinet/speaker response voiced for bass-guitar frequencies.
best_for: pairing with bass amp voicings for rock or studio bass tone

Large Cab.what_it_does: Larger multi-speaker cabinet response (typically 4x12), generally fuller and louder-feeling with more low-end authority and projection.
best_for: rock, hard rock and metal rigs wanting a bigger, more aggressive low end
watch_out: can feel loose or boomy on amps that are already bass-heavy

Small Cab.what_it_does: Smaller speaker cabinet response (combo-sized, 1x8 to 2x12), generally tighter, more focused and more midrange-forward.
best_for: vintage combo tones, clean/edge-of-breakup rigs, and any tone wanting a tighter low end
watch_out: may feel thin under very high-gain, low-tuned material compared with a 4x12

character: defined entirely by the loaded IR file
best_for: reproducing a specific real or captured cabinet/mic combination
watch_out: do not select unless the user has explicitly supplied or referenced their own IR

EQ.what_it_does: Shapes bass, mid and treble balance, either correcting a tone or fitting it into a mix.
character: corrective or tone-sculpting rather than an obvious effect
best_for: fitting a tone into a mix
watch_out: extreme boosts can sound harsh, boomy or unnatural

Chorus.what_it_does: Adds a gently detuned, modulated double around the dry signal for width and shimmer.
watch_out: high depth/rate can blur pitch definition and attack, especially on chords

Flanger.what_it_does: Creates a sweeping comb-filter effect from a short, modulated delay mixed with the dry signal.
watch_out: deep settings can be disorienting or overwhelming under a full mix

Phaser.what_it_does: Creates moving phase-cancellation notches for a liquid, swirling motion.
watch_out: fast rates can clash with busy, note-dense playing
deep settings can interrupt sustained notes or chords

Vibrato.what_it_does: Modulates pitch without the dry doubled signal that chorus adds.
best_for: expressive pitch wobble on sustained notes
watch_out: deep settings can sound seasick on chordal material

Delay.what_it_does: Repeats the signal after a chosen time interval; choose time, feedback, and mix to add space without obscuring notes.
character: ranges from tight rhythmic echoes to spacious ambient trails depending on the model and settings
watch_out: high feedback or mix can obscure the original notes and clutter a busy mix

Reverb.what_it_does: Simulates an acoustic space; use mix and decay to place the guitar without washing it out.
character: ranges from tight room ambience to long, expansive tails depending on the model
watch_out: long decay or high mix can wash out fast passages and blur note definition

SnapTone.what_it_does: Plays back an imported tone capture in place of a modelled amp and cab.
character: defined entirely by whatever was captured
best_for: reproducing a specific captured amp/cab/pedal chain
watch_out: a populated SnapTone slot generally replaces the need for a separate AMP and CAB block; an empty slot has no usable tone and must not be selected
